children: Colombia's central bank is expected to raise its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points on Friday to 12.50%, according to a Reuters poll of analysts, in what would likely be its last increase this year as inflation expectations rise.
Seventeen analysts in the poll forecast a quarter-point increase, 13 expected the bank to hold at 12.25%, and one projected a 75-basis-point rise to 13.00%
Colombia's annual inflation hit 6.29% through September, more than double the central bank's 3% target.
The El Niño weather phenomenon has begun pressuring food prices, which could worsen due to drought-related fires, said BNP Paribas, which projects a 25 basis point bump.
A minority of analysts expect the rate to remain stable, citing weakening economic activity indicators for July and August, according to the poll.
The market expects Colombia to miss its inflation target for the sixth consecutive year in 2026, as well as in 2027.
If the majority prediction does indeed take place at Friday's policy meeting, this would be the second consecutive rate increase, totaling a raise of 325 basis points so far in 2026.
The majority of the market believes the interest rate will close this year at 12.50%, with expectations for end-2027 at 11%.

"Economic indicators for July and August show a slowdown, especially following a slight decline in core inflation the previous month, which may lead the (central) bank to keep the rate steady,” BBVA said in an analysts' note.
There will be no monetary policy meeting in November.
